newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts' comments on DSM 1996 results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' comments on DSM 1996 results.

text.p: Dutch petrochemicals group DSM NV reported that its 1996 net profit fell to 720 million guilders from 1.07 billion in 1995. Despite this the firm said it was raising its dividend to nine guilders per share from eight. It said it expected its results for the first half of 1997 to be comparable to those in the same period of 1996.
Below is a collection of analysts' comments on DSM's results:

"I expect full-year profits in 1997 to be higher than in 1996. DSM should profit from higher prices and an economic upturn. The combination of those two things will work out well for DSM. I am sticking to my buy recommendation for DSM, but it is too early to upgrade our earnings forecast as I need to look at the figures more closely first."

"Earnings from hydrocarbons and polymers were above my expectations, so pressure on margins was not so great despite the unfavourable development in prices. That will have a positive follow-through effect in 1997. I had previously been expecting slightly lower earnings in 1997, but now I expect a slight increase compared with 1996. The other thing I'm positive about is the dividend policy... DSM plans to buy back shares to pay out a dividend in shares which will be tax-free for Dutch investors. I had thought they would pay an unchanged dividend of eight guilders, but the actual payout is a guilder higher."
